title: DDIA 3 · STORAGE & RETRIEVAL
subtitle: How a database actually stores bytes.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Kleppmann). Read the book.

blocks.text: Old values pile up, so background compaction merges segments and keeps only the latest value per key.
A read checks the memtable, then SSTables from newest to oldest. Bloom filters skip files that can't contain the key, so reads cost more than writes.
Updates overwrite the page in place, after writing to the WAL first so a crash mid-write can be repaired. A full page splits in two.

blocks.text: Each index slows down every write and uses disk. Index for the hot read queries you named, not for every column.

panels.label: OLTP VS OLAP, AND THE STAR SCHEMA

blocks.text: Dimension tables hold the who, what, where, and when. Queries filter on dimensions and aggregate facts: "revenue by city by weekday".
Values in one column look alike, so they compress very well. Vectorized CPU processing on top makes these scans 10–100× faster.

items: "LSM-tree storage: writes are sequential appends to memtable + commit log, so write throughput is very high.
